title: What Shall We Ask of God in Prayer
description: What Shall We Ask of God in Prayer in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 32, “A Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: What shall we ask of God in prayer? What-ev-er good we want; What-ev-er man may seek to share, Or God in wis-dom grant.

lines: What shall we ask of God in prayer?
Whatever good we want;
Whatever man may seek to share,
Or God in wisdom grant.
Father of all our mercies, — Thou
In whom we move and live!
Hear us in heaven, Thy dwelling, now,
And answer, and forgive.
When harassed by ten thousand foes,
Our helplessness we feel,
O, give the weary soul repose,
The wounded spirit heal!
When dire temptations gather round,
And threaten or allure,
By storm or calm, in Thee be found
A refuge strong and sure.
When age advances, may we grow
In faith, in hope, and love;
And walk in holiness below
To holiness above.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
